newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government to start budget debate Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: Polish government to start budget debate Oct 15.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry has already submitted its 1997 budget draft to the government, which will start debating the bill on October 15, a finance ministry spokeswoman said on Friday.
"The government will start working on the budget at its next meeting on October 15," Anna Sobocinska told Reuters.
The ministry declined to disclose the details of the draft and it was not immediately clear whether its key parameters differed from a general budget outline approved by the government in July.
The outline assumed a shortfall slightly below this year's planned deficit of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
The ministry has also said the outline was tailored to make it possible to reach next year's inflation target of 13 percent while maintaining economic growth of about 5.5 percent.
The government has until the end of October to submit its final draft to parliament and deputies will have three months to pass the budget.
